title: Python Basics Arcade
intro: Time to test what you've learned! Predict outputs, fix broken code, and build code blocks. Get them right on the first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: Run this line. What shows up on the screen?
rounds.explain: print shows whatever is inside the quotation marks.

rounds.prompt: This line is broken! Pick the fix.
options: Add the missing closing quote: print("Coding is fun")
Add a number at the end
rounds.explain: Every opening quote needs a closing quote, or Python gets confused!

rounds.prompt: Which line stores the number 7 in a box called score?
rounds.explain: Variables work like labelled boxes: the name goes on the left, the value on the right.
x is 5 and y is 3, so x + y becomes 8.

rounds.prompt: What kind of data is "42" (with the quotation marks)?
rounds.explain: Quotation marks turn anything into text, a string, even if it looks like a number.

rounds.prompt: Match each Python piece to what it does.

pairs.right: Puts a value into a variable

rounds.explain: print() displays things, = stores a value in a variable, quotes make a string, and a bare number like 7 is an int.

rounds.prompt: Build the code: store a name, then greet it.
rounds.explain: First create the variable, then you can use it on the next line.
